# dsh-readme
**English** · 简体中文

Read one text file — a team conventions file, a project's `AgentsReadMe.md`, a
style guide — and inj

ect its contents into the system prompt of **every** agent
before that agent's first model request.

The file's rules then apply for the whole
session, in that session's main agent and in every subagen

ules then apply for the whole
session, in that session's main agent and in every subagent it spawns.
## Why a system prompt section and not a message

DSH assembles the system prompt before each model step, from ordered sections. A
section's text may

be a function, so it is re-evaluated per step. Mounting the file
as a section therefore needs no ses

sion hooks at all: there is no step that could
send a request without first assembling the section,

so "read before the first run"
is a structural guarantee rather than a race the plugin tries to win.

It also survives context compression. A file fed in as a chat message can be
summarised away half an
hour later; a system-prompt section cannot.

or point the profile at it by hand — add the package to `dependencies` and to
`dsh.profile.bundles`
in the profile's `package.json`, then reinstall:

Restart DSH afterwards: bundle rows are read at startup.

Or install it straight from this repository (a `git:` dependency; the `file:`
form above is what a l
ocal checkout uses):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then tell the plugin which file to read — see Configure.
## If the plugin stops loading

A profile selects its plugins by name in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The plugin manager
rebuilds that lis

t whenever it installs or removes **any** package, and it keeps an
existing entry only while `node_m

odules/<name>/package.json` still declares
`dsh.bundle.patch`. A package directory that is momentari

ly absent — an interrupted
install, a reinstall, a manual cleanup — therefore drops out of the list

silently,
and it does not come back on its own. The plugin stays in `dependencies`, its
settings sta
y in the profile patch, and nothing loads it.

Two ways to see it. In the app, the constraint section is simply absent from the
prompt. From a shel

prompt. From a shell:

The script reads the profile (not a checkout of this repository), reports the
dependency, the bundle

row, the installed copy, the patch and the configured file,
and exits non-zero when one of them is

wrong. If the row is the missing piece, add
the name back to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's

`package.json` and restart.
The same condition shows up at startup as:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Configure

The plugin ships its own configuration page, registered on the plugin page's
`plugins.row.config` se

at: open **Settings → Plugins**, open the bundle that lists
this row, then use `Configure` on the `d

sh-readme` row to edit the path and save.
The write goes to the active profile's patch document and

needs no restart — the
next prompt assembly reads the new file.

The page reads and writes the form state the host hands it, so validation, revision
conflicts and th

e read-only fallback are the host's, not the plugin's: a write
carries a `revision` and a stale one

is reported as a conflict; a field already
fixed by the profile patch or a command-line overlay show

s as read-only instead of
being silently dropped.
Every field can also be written by hand in the profile patch:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Inject at all. Off means the plugin writes nothing into the prompt. |
| `path
` | `""` | The file. Supports `~`, `$VAR`, `${VAR}`, `%VAR%`. A relative path resolves against the *

*session's** working directory. Empty means "not configured yet", and the plugin stays silent. |
| `
maxBytes` | `32768` | Cap on injected text, 1024–4194304. A longer file is truncated **and the model
is told so**, because a model that assumes it read the whole file will confidently violate the part

that was cut. |
| `reloadOnChange` | `true` | Re-read when the file changes. Off pins the first rea
d for the life of the mount, which keeps the prompt byte-identical across steps and friendlier to pr

ompt caching. |
| `onMissing` | `notice` | What to inject when the file cannot be read: `notice` put

s one line in the prompt telling the model to say so; `silent` injects nothing. |
| `order` | `520`
| Position in the prompt. 520 is after the plan policy (500) and before the team policy (600). |

Each setting can also come from the environment (`DSH_README_ENABLED`,
`DSH_README_PATH`, `DSH_READM

E_ORDER`, `DSH_README_MAX_BYTES`,
`DSH_README_RELOAD_ON_CHANGE`, `DSH_README_ON_MISSING`), which is

useful for a
headless deployment with no panel. Precedence: configuration wins, the environment
[该节后

ul for a
headless deployment with no panel. Precedence: configuration wins, the environment
[该节后续省略]
## What the model sees
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The framing is deliberate. "Here is a file" reads as reference material the model
may weigh against

its defaults, which is exactly what a constraints file exists to
prevent; the header instead states

where the authority comes from, what wins a
conflict, and — the line that keeps the injection afford

able — that the file is not
to be echoed back.
## Behaviour details

- **Read lazily, on the first assembly.** Not at plugin load. A session started
hours after install

sees the file as it is now.
- **Cached by `(path, size, mtime)`.** An unchanged file costs one `stat

` per step,
not a read.
- **Missing, empty, binary, directory, unreadable:** each has its own state.

An
empty file or an unconfigured path injects nothing at all — injecting an empty
header would spen

d tokens on every step to say nothing.
- **Binary files are refused** (a NUL in the first 8 KiB), so

pointing `path` at a
zip by mistake produces a notice instead of mojibake in the prompt.
- **Trunca

tion cuts on a UTF-8 boundary**, never mid-character, and a BOM is
stripped.
[该节后续省略]
